articles.title: A textural moment: why the fashion world is falling in love with opera coats
articles.summary: From Jennifer Lawrence to Kate Moss, the fuzz-trimmed garments are proving popular with celebrities, while others are DIY-ing their way into the trend. While puffer jackets have dominated winter wardrobes for years, this winter an alternative is emerging: the fuzz-trimmed opera coat.
body: Originally worn over formal evening gowns, new interpretations come in floor-grazing and cropped styles and are being worn with everything from minidresses to jeans.

Jennifer Lawrence wore a Dior opera coat, complete with a furry shawl collar, to the premiere of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping this week, while Kendall Jenner has been photographed in a maxi yellow version, which she wore with slouchy trousers. Having fuzzed their way down various catwalks, Staud, DÔEN, Zara, Next, Free People and Marks & Spencer are all stocking the new “it” coats.
Rixo’s floral embroidered and faux-fur trimmed version, worn by both Lawrence and Kate Moss, has sold out several times.
“I think the appeal of these coats is that they feel both luxurious and wonderfully nostalgic,” says Orlagh McCloskey, the cofounder and creative director of the London-based brand.

articles.title: Vitamin D, fiber and flavor: how healthy are mushrooms?
articles.summary: Experts say there are many reasons to boost our consumption of mushrooms and incorporate them into our diets. Mushrooms aren’t quite as popular in the US as they are in other parts of the world.
body: People in the US also don’t consume as wide a variety of mushrooms as other parts of the world, says Dr Krystle Zuniga, a board-certified oncology dietitian based in Austin, Texas. “I often think of them as a forgotten vegetable,” she says, though she clarifies they are technically fungi.
Yet there’s good reason to boost our consumption of mushrooms and incorporate different varieties into our diets. Here’s what experts say about the health benefits of mushrooms.

“The selling points for mushrooms for many years were that they taste good, and they don’t have any bad stuff in them,” says Dr Robert Beelman, professor emeritus of food science and director of the Center for Plant and Mushroom Foods for Health at Penn State University. “There’s very little fat, no sugar, very few calories.”

Mushrooms’ savoury, umami flavor also makes them a particularly good option for anyone looking to eat less meat. “I often recommend replacing up to 50% of ground meat with chopped mushrooms for meatballs, tacos or meat sauce recipes,” says Marisa Moore, a registered nutritionist based in Atlanta.

articles.title: What 8 Cool Food People Outsource for Thanksgiving
articles.summary: This story was previously published as part of that series. Subscribe to Eater Today to see more of our editors’ boldest opinions about dining culture writ large. A few Novembers ago, I had a mild crash out over puff pastry.
body: If you buy something from a link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Then I remembered the puff pastry. For some reason, I attached a moral imperative to the idea of making the whole pie from scratch, and spent the next two weeks poring over puff pastry recipes that felt like casual guides to wizard-tier alchemy. I loved to cook, but I simply wasn’t a big baker. (I also didn’t own a food processor, unless you counted my Magic Bullet.) My mother eventually brought me down to Earth. “Just buy it,” she told me over the phone, undoubtedly rolling her eyes. “Everyone knows it’s a pain in the butt.” Even the Barefoot Contessa herself, she reminded me, famously avoids the time-consuming task ( “Nobody wants to make puff pastry!” ).

Those words set me free. Once I realized that I could outsource my puff pastry, and the source of my Thanksgiving stress, I was finally able to relax and enjoy the holiday. Folks take pride in their Turkey Day dishes, as they should, but there’s nothing wrong with accepting a little help.

articles.title: The Unstoppable Cecilia Vicuña
articles.summary: This fall, the Chilean artist and poet has shows on both sides of the country, at the Museum of Contemporary Art in Los Angeles and Lehmann Maupin in New York City.
body: It’s a perfect fall day, bright and brisk, when I meet the Chilean artist and poet Cecilia Vicuña at her studio in Tribeca, just a few blocks away from the loft she’s lived in for the last 46 years.

As someone so closely tethered to the natural world, Vicuña wishes we could go outside and enjoy it. We can, I offer—there’s no reason to stay cooped up inside for our entire conversation. Grinning, she agrees to show me her studio first. “And then we seek the sun.”

Vicuña, 78, is a seeker of many things: truth, justice, beauty, connection with people and the earth. For more than five decades she has brought attention to under-recognized voices through her sculptures, paintings, poems, videos, sound installations, and performances. For many of those years she worked in relative obscurity, known in certain avant-garde and activist circles in New York and South America, but unacknowledged by the establishment. But the global art world woke up to her brilliance about a decade ago, especially when her quipus —hanging sculptures made from wool that nod to the ancient Andean knot systems—attracted attention at Documenta 14 in Germany and Greece.

articles.title: Inside the Confetti-Filled Opening Night of ‘Much Ado About Nothing,’ Starring Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell
articles.summary: William Shakespeare’s “Much Ado About Nothing” arrived at the Winter Garden Theatre on Thursday with an explosion of fuchsia confetti, a giant inflatable heart, and seriously impressive dance moves from Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell.
body: Forget the traditional opening-night fanfare. If love is a many-splendored thing, apparently it’s also bright pink and best enjoyed with a ’90s dance anthem blasting in the background.

Following its successful run in London’s West End, the production crossed the Atlantic with Hiddleston and Atwell reprising their roles as Benedick and Beatrice, two sharp-witted characters who trade barbs before falling in love. At the show’s helm is acclaimed British director Jamie Lloyd, known for his bold, contemporary reimaginings of classic plays and musicals. With Much Ado About Nothing, he’s given Shakespeare’s romantic comedy a gloriously over-the-top makeover.

The party started long before the curtain rose. From the moment guests stepped into the Winter Garden, ushers danced down the aisles, greeting theatergoers as though they were arriving at the hottest club. Cynthia Nixon, Rachel Zegler, Bryan Cranston, Claire Danes, Angela Bassett, Bob Odenkirk, Hugh Dancy, and Busy Philipps were among the familiar faces in the crowd, which had enough star power to rival the theatrical fireworks unfolding onstage.

articles.title: The Couple Created a Giant Sunflower Walkway For Their Multicultural Sun Valley Wedding
articles.summary: Set at an Idaho 4-H camp, Parker Selman and Karan Rai’s weekend celebration blended Punjabi, Hindu, Jewish, and Episcopalian traditions—plus a custom bridal gown inspired by 1955 Christian Dior.
body: The couple got engaged on a crisp autumn walk around Governors Island—Parker’s favorite spot in the city. She owns and operates a wedding photography business, and as they strolled along, she asked to take a picture of Karan on her medium-format camera with their apartment building and skyline in the background. “While I was snapping the photo, he got down on one knee,” she says, “and I had the privilege of capturing my own proposal.” They rode the ferry back to Manhattan and went to Della’s, a local wine bar, where their families and friends were waiting to celebrate.

Two months later, she proposed back. “While we were walking in Sun Valley, I requested he take a picture of me sitting in the snow with our dog Grumpy,” she says. "I proposed the same way he proposed to me, the moment captured on my Rolleiflex.” Parker used diamonds and emeralds from her late great-grandmother’s engagement ring and gold from Karan’s late grandmother’s earrings to create his signet ring.

articles.title: The Best Hotels Near Disneyland Paris With Cinderella Suites, 'Toy Story'–Themed Rooms, and Quaint Cottages
articles.summary: Here's where to stay near the park to maximize your time—and shorten your commute between the airport and the city.
body: Located just 40 minutes from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport, Disneyland Paris is the ideal place to begin a Parisian vacation or say au revoir before returning home. Disneyland Paris's two theme parks, Disneyland Park and Disney Adventure World, pair timeless charm with an ease you'll never find stateside. Here, you can sip Champagne in front of Sleeping Beauty's castle—or visit a dragon beneath it—while filling your days with delightful architecture, unprecedented thrills, and the wildest wilderness ride Disney's ever built (Big Thunder Mountain!).

There's also never been a better time to visit. Walt Disney Studios Park's March 2026 transformation into the new Disney Adventure World brought a drone-filled nighttime show, Avengers coaster, and even a Frozen -themed land featuring a lifelike Olaf robot to its once-faltering second gate. Now, between Fantasyland classics and futuristic favorites, there's something new and thrilling for the entire family to experience.
